killedByTerminal.firstMatch: T13: the name says Search and the ordinal says Exit, so a fallback ranking would press either Enter or F3.
killedByTerminal.countQuorum: T14: a grid field's accessible name is derived from its prompt, so role-name and label-anchored are one piece of evidence.
killedByTerminal.checkpointFirst: T03/T04: the status band carries the business outcome while the screen is still the inquiry screen.
killedByTerminal.noDelta: T08: a repaint that never arrived leaves the previous screen in place, and the checkpoint alone cannot notice that no effect occurred.
killedByTerminal.nearestMatch: T06/T08: a torn read and a stale screen both share words with declared outcome codes, so nearest-string matching invents an answer.

outOfReachOnTerminal.noAssert: Needs a target that resolves correctly and is still the wrong thing. This TUI fixture has account rows keyed by suffix and each row belongs to the member it just looked up, so the assert-failed shape is not observable here.
outOfReachOnTerminal.noSettleGate: Observationally indistinguishable on this terminal surface. The readiness signal is silence; the measured torn repaint is also silent, so the driver reports settled true even on a half-painted frame. The checkpoint, not the settle flag, is the enforceable gate here.
outOfReachOnTerminal.noContinuity: Needs the application to land on a different member's record. This fixture echoes back the account number it was given; producing the divergence would require a fixture that lies about which member it opened.
outOfReachOnTerminal.noProvenance: Needs the same validation banner over a caller argument and over an artifact literal. This TUI flow fills one caller-supplied field, so those two provenance rows collapse into one observable case.

rows.description: takes the first descriptor that resolved instead of requiring agreement
counts descriptors instead of counting distinct evidence sources
dispatches without re-deriving the identity of the node it is about to touch
classifies against whatever is on screen, settled or not
verifies the checkpoint before looking for declared business outcomes
verifies that a member detail page loaded, never that it is the right member's
trusts the checkpoint to notice that the action did anything at all
promotes an unmatched screen to the closest declared outcome by string similarity
classifies a validation error without asking where the rejected value came from
